name: Non-rechargeable cells (lithium and alkaline)
summary: Single-use cells: alkaline AA to D and 9V, and long-life lithium cells in alarms, defibrillators, cameras and meters.
uses: Meters and sensors that sip power for years
identify: Labelled alkaline, lithium or "do not recharge". Lithium primaries are often CR123A, 2/3A or sealed 10-year packs; 3.0–3.6V per cell.
test: Measure open-circuit voltage: alkaline above about 1.4V and lithium above about 3.0V still have useful charge. Check again under a small load.

decay.note: Lithium primaries lose 1–2% a year in storage; alkalines a few percent but leak with age.
